The di- and mono-oleyl esters of 3-(N-phenylamino)-1,2-propanediol are the compounds most strongly associated with case-related oil. They are hydrolysed by pancreatic lipase like a triglyceride, absorbed from the gut, and distributed to organs - which is what makes a systemic disease from an ingested compound.
